title: coap_keys_format: provider-less fingerprint fallback emits 64-bit hex under a SHA256: label
description: Discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-at2y (security review). Pre-existing, not a migration regression: when no SHA-256 provider is configured, lichen_key_pubkey_fingerprint() (coap_keys_format.c #else branch) returns a 64-bit truncated-pubkey hex string with a 'SHA256:' scheme prefix — a consumer doing spec 17.5.5 TOFU out-of-band comparison gets a silent algorithm/length downgrade presented as a SHA-256 fingerprint. Distinguishable only by length/charset (16 hex + '...' vs 43 base64 chars). Options: emit a distinct scheme (e.g. PUBKEYPREFIX64:) from the fallback, or return -ENOTSUP so provider-less builds fail loudly like coap_slot_coord.c does. Note the Kconfig imply only papers over this for default configs; a KEYS=y + provider=n build still reaches the fallback.
close_reason: Fixed: provider-less fingerprint fallback now fails closed with -ENOTSUP instead of emitting a 64-bit truncated-pubkey hex under a 'SHA256:' label (spec 17.5.5 TOFU downgrade). buf[0]='\0' hoisted to function entry so all error returns (after arg validation) leave buf a valid empty string — coap_keys_cbor.c ignores the return and would otherwise strlen() uninitialized stack. Header doc updated to document the buffer-on-error contract and the new -ENOTSUP return. Callers verified fail-closed: coap_keys_cbor encodes empty fp_str (0x60), coap_config identity_short_fingerprint short-circuits on length check. 3x codereview delegated to kimi-k3: correctness (1 finding: fp_str uninitialized → fixed buf[0] at entry), security (1 finding: -EIO/-ENOMEM paths left buf uninitialized → same fix), edge-cases (1 finding: doc overpromised NUL-termination on -EINVAL → doc scoped). Tests: coap_keys 37/37 PASS on heft native_sim (provider branch via LICHEN_LINK→MBEDTLS_SHA256); ENOTSUP path is Zephyr-config-only and exercised by gcc -fsyntax-only. coap_config test app build failure is pre-existing (bead 0whw zcbor stub), unrelated.
